fileStructure: app/admin.py: support-console helpers for account recovery. app/auth.py: unchanged; login remains the only session source. app/models.py: User gains must_change_password.

tasks.title: Support console can find an account by email
tasks.specExcerpt: R2 — Requesting a reset. The user is looked up by email address. An address with no account must not reveal whether an account exists.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_admin_lookup -v → OK (2 tests): a known address returns the User, an unknown one returns None
steps: write tests/test_admin_lookup.py for the known and unknown address
run it → ModuleNotFoundError: app.admin
add app/admin.py delegating to store.get_user_by_email
run it → OK (2 tests), commit

tasks.title: Support agent issues a temporary password
tasks.produces: issue_temp_password(user_id: int) -> str — writes User.password_hash with a random 12-character temporary and sets must_change_password
tasks.consumes: find_account from app/admin.py; hash_password and save_user
tasks.specExcerpt: R5 — Setting the new password. The account's stored credential becomes the new password and the user can immediately sign in with it. `app/auth.py:login` reads `User.password_hash`; that is the field a successful reset has to leave behind.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_admin_temp -v → OK (3 tests): issue_temp_password returns a 12-character string, auth.login(email, temp) returns a session token, and must_change_password is True
steps: write tests/test_admin_temp.py whose central assertion is that login with the temporary succeeds
run it → AttributeError: issue_temp_password
add must_change_password to models.User with a False default
implement issue_temp_password: 12 chars via ''.join(secrets.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(12)), then hash_password, save_user
run it → OK (3 tests), commit

tasks.title: Every agent-initiated reset is audited
tasks.produces: audit_reset(agent_id: int, user_id: int) -> None; RESET_LOG list
tasks.specExcerpt: R1 — Token issuance. A reset is single-use and attributable: each issuance is recorded against the account it was issued for.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_admin_audit -v → OK (2 tests): issuing a temporary appends exactly one RESET_LOG entry carrying both ids, and a failed lookup appends none
steps: write tests/test_admin_audit.py asserting the entry count and its fields
run it → AttributeError: audit_reset
implement audit_reset and call it from issue_temp_password
run it → OK (2 tests), commit

tasks.title: A must-change account changes its own password after signing in
tasks.produces: change_password(user_id: int, current: str, new: str) -> bool — clears must_change_password on success
tasks.consumes: must_change_password from app/models.py; verify_password and hash_password from app/auth.py
tasks.specExcerpt: R5 — Setting the new password. Given the account and a new password, the stored credential becomes that password and the user can immediately sign in with it.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_forced_change -v → OK (3 tests): change_password with the correct current password returns True and auth.login with the new password succeeds; a wrong current password returns False; must_change_password is False afterwards
steps: write tests/test_forced_change.py covering both the correct and wrong current password
run it → AttributeError: change_password
implement change_password: verify_password against the stored hash, then hash_password, clear the flag, save_user
run it → OK (3 tests), commit

tasks.title: Issuing a temporary clears a failed-attempt lockout
tasks.produces: issue_temp_password additionally clears User.locked_reason when it equals 'failed-attempts'
tasks.consumes: issue_temp_password from app/admin.py; User.locked_reason from app/models.py
tasks.specExcerpt: R6 — Lockout interaction. A reset clears `User.locked_reason` when it was set by failed sign-in attempts, so a user is not locked out of the account they just recovered.
tasks.testCycle: python3 -m unittest tests.test_admin_lockout -v → OK (2 tests): a user with locked_reason='failed-attempts' can log in with the temporary; a user with locked_reason='fraud-review' still cannot
steps: write tests/test_admin_lockout.py for both lockout reasons
run it → the fraud-review case passes, the failed-attempts case fails
add the conditional clear inside issue_temp_password before save_user
run it → OK (2 tests), commit
